served.bankWhy: Paragraph 8 introduces Pauling as the example Watson and Crick were following: guess the structure by building a model, then test it against the data. The alpha helix is there as proof that the method could work.

proof.quote: Following the example of Linus Pauling, who had found the alpha helix of proteins in 1951 by building models

distractorNotes: Contradicted: paragraph 2 says Avery's experiment of 1944 changed the mood in favor of DNA over proteins.
Wrong cause: Bragg's order followed the failed model of November 1951, not Pauling's protein work.
Contradicted: Pauling's DNA model of 1953 shared the flaw of the first Cambridge attempt.
Outside the passage: the author never compares the two helices.

answer.text: identify the method of model building that Watson and Crick were imitating
answer.line: Sentence 2 opens "Following the example of Linus Pauling." He found a helix by building models, and Watson and Crick did the same.

steps: Read the sentence the name sits in. It opens with "Following the example of Linus Pauling".
Pauling found the alpha helix by building models. Watson and Crick guessed first and tested after: the same method.
Why name Pauling? For his method. The helix is not being compared with anything.

choices.text: show that proteins had already been proven to be the true carriers of heredity
choices.note: Proteins only looked like the better candidate, paragraph 2, and Avery's 1944 work pointed to DNA. Nothing proves proteins carry heredity.

choices.text: explain why Bragg ordered Watson and Crick to stop working on DNA
choices.note: Pauling does come into Bragg's story, but at the other end: his three-chain model got the pair let back in, sentence 6. The order itself followed their dropped model.

choices.text: identify the method of model building that Watson and Crick were imitating
choices.note: Following the example of: build the model first, test it against the data after.

choices.text: suggest that Pauling had already solved the structure of DNA by 1951
choices.note: Pauling's DNA model of early 1953 had the same flaw as their first one. He had not solved it.

choices.text: contrast the alpha helix of proteins with the double helix of DNA
choices.note: Both are helices, but the sentence cites Pauling for how he worked, not to compare the two shapes.
